text.p: ImmuDyne Inc said Wednesday that the hearing scheduled for June 18 before the 225th Judicial District Court, Bexar County, San Antonio, Texas to enforce an agreement and related summary judgment involving Carmel Research Inc has been postponed in part as a result of the filing by Carmel of Chapter 11 Bankruptcy on June 17.

Management of ImmuDyne expected that enforcement of the agreement and summary judgment would have required Carmel, an Immudyne shareholder, to turn over to ImmuDyne 3.25 million shares of ImmuDyne common stock.

ImmuDyne would have been required to issue 1.55 million shares of common stock to Mark McLaughlin, a shareholder, and his attorneys, and would have retired 1.7 million such shares, all in accordance with the summary judgment.
The effect of this ruling and Carmel's bankruptcy is being reviewed by ImmuDyne.
On June 18, the court ordered ImmuDyne to deliver to McLaughlin the $100,000 of the royalties accumulated from November 1996 to present, otherwise due to Carmel, pursuant to the summary judgment.
ImmuDyne said the issue of being able to pay these moneys is clouded by the Carmel bankruptcy.
In a separate matter, the company said it received notice of a lawsuit filed by shareholder Byron Donzis against the company relating to the non payment of certain consulting fees.
The complaint against ImmuDyne was filed in the 2nd Judicial District Court of the State of Nevada.
The company said it is evaluating the claims and intends to vigorously defend such allegations.
